note: [agent-bulk] verdict shower 79054 (pdg 11, kine_charge 329.8 MeV, 17 seg, 68.9 cm) -- the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object. Passed over 9018: pdg 13, 197.9 cm, kine_charge 307.1 but kine_best 424.8 MeV, i.e. higher than 79054 on kine_best -- it is the muon, not an EM shower. Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames (r95 154.8 cm, correction 20): the blue star sits exactly on the apex where the muon 9018, the 20.7 cm pdg-211 track 9020 and the shower fan converge, at two azimuths and at el+60 -- vertex is good. Membership triple-check passes: nseg 17 = owner-grouped 17 = cmp_div 17, and the owner groups sum to 38 segments = the whole event, so the following is a complete statement: the ONLY unowned segment in the event is 9020, and it sits at 9.5 cm / 176.5 deg, i.e. directly behind the shower start -- it does not belong. Every other non-member is either the muon chain (9011/9013/9023 at 28-36 deg, forward but well off axis), the second gamma 83073 (70-77 deg), or a sub-20 MeV fragment that is the seed of its own shower (correction 16). Members are a single cone, single apex: 0-96.7 cm at 0.0-25.8 deg, with a 22 cm internal gap (dense multi-point core at 9.5-39 cm from the vertex, nothing between 39 and 61 cm, then 2-3-point stubs out to 106 cm). Same shape as pilot 2.3 evt284791, and 'correct' here means the same thing: nothing is missing. WHAT THE OWNER COULD REVERSE: 8 of the 17 members lie beyond 60 cm, 7 of those 8 are pdg 13/211, and two (36034 at 79.5 cm / 25.8 deg, 26024 at 96.7 cm / 13.7 deg) are tier '-' i.e. outside the pass-1 box, pulled in by pass4_angle (direct). Their charge is negligible (2-3 points each), but if the owner counts that reach as over-reach this event reads over-clustered. I deliberately recorded NO out-marks on them (pilot 5: an OUT mark on a member is read downstream as the remove-this statement and would contradict the 'correct' radio). One thing I could not attribute: a striped point-cloud blob about 88 cm out, ~10 cm off the muon, that carries no skeleton segment of its own; the cloud readout says all 4393 drawn points are the single neutrino-candidate cluster 9, so there is no per-point owner to test it against -- named, not judged. pi0: the reco's own pairing (showers[].pio_id group 0) is 79054 + 83073 and I confirm it as the only sensible pair in the event; stored as the same pair. Mass 114.3 MeV on the vertex convention, 88.0 MeV on the axis convention -- both inside the code's accept window, but 21 MeV under 135 and the two conventions disagree by 26 MeV, consistent with 83073 (38.1 MeV, 3 seg, 7.3 cm) being an incompletely clustered low-energy gamma; nothing large is available nearby to add to it, so I did not call it under-clustered. NOT LOOKED AT: the 7 out-of-scope showers, all <= 17.7 MeV (9016 17.7, then 5.5, 5.4, 2.5, 1.7, 1.4, 1.1). This verdict is a statement about clustering of 79054 and is silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] verdict shower 16055 (pdg 11, kine_charge 142.1 MeV, 8 seg, 30.4 cm) -- the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; nothing in the event outranks it on either energy (16059 is pdg 211 at 83.3). Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames at two azimuths (correction 20): r95 is 277 cm here so the vtx-* set is framed at +-346 cm and the vertex region is a few pixels in it. The star sits at the convergence of the 16055 prong going one way and the 16059 (orange) + 16060 (green) prongs going the other, with the 16054 stub between -- vertex is OK. Membership triple-check passes: nseg 8 = owner-grouped 8 = cmp_div 8, and the owner groups sum to 27 segments = the whole event, so there is NO unowned/grey segment anywhere in this event; every non-member of 16055 is either a member of another shower or the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower (correction 16). Decomposing each member's (dist, angle) into along/transverse: the body is 0-20 cm along with transverse spread up to 16 cm (a compact, wide 142 MeV shower start), then a 45 cm void with no charge at all, then three 2-point stubs (74050 / 75051 / 76052, pdg 13, 0.3-0.4 cm each) at 65-72 cm along and 29-33 cm transverse. WHAT THE OWNER COULD REVERSE: on the acceptance plot those three sit INSIDE the pass-1 box (<=80 cm, <=30 deg) as tier-1 pass3_cone members, so the gate took them by design and their charge is negligible -- but a 45 cm void plus ~3 Moliere radii of transverse offset is not EM shower tail, and if the owner counts that this event reads over-clustered. THE ONE UNDER-REACH: 73049 (pdg 11, 2.7 MeV, 3 points, 1.0 cm) sits at 21.9 cm / 47.9 deg, only 3.6 cm from the nearest member point, and on the acceptance plot it is the lone blue circle sitting between accepted members at (18.0 cm, 46.2 deg) and (19.8 cm, 54.8 deg) -- the exclusion looks arbitrary. It is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower rather than grey charge, and at 1.9% of 142.1 MeV I did not upgrade the verdict; named so the owner can. I recorded NO marks in either direction, to keep the record consistent with the 'correct' radio (pilot 5). OTHER SHOWERS: 16059 (pdg 211, 83.3 MeV, 20.3 cm) and 16060 (pdg 11, 46.9 MeV, 2 seg) leave the vertex collinearly and 16001 (owned by 16059) sits at 18.7 cm / 14.7 deg inside 16060's cone -- these two may be one prong split into a pion and a 47 MeV shower, and 16060 also carries a lone member at 44.8 cm / 11.5 deg across a comparable void. That is a finding about 16059/16060 and I did not resolve it; it does not bear on 16055, which is on the far side of the vertex from both. pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event'. The capture's auto-slotted pair [16055, 16060] is the correction-3 artifact, not a reco pairing, and the two are 162.9 deg apart i.e. back-to-back through the vertex -- not a pi0 topology, nothing stored. The kine_pio_* block (a BDT feature, not a pairing) names 26.0 + 142.1 at 157.4 deg and does not close (119.2 vs stored 66.2). NOT LOOKED AT: the 7 out-of-scope showers, all <= 17.3 MeV. This verdict is about clustering of 16055 and is silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] verdict shower 64033 (pdg 11, kine_charge 154.0 MeV, 6 seg, 21.2 cm) -- the only pdg-11 object in scope; the other in-scope entry 53018 is pdg 2212 and flagged 'conn 4: dropped by the PF tree'. Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames (r95 260.7 cm): at el+60 the event is a clean V of two long unowned grey tracks meeting exactly on the star -- 16001 (pdg 13, 284.1 cm, member points 0.0-277.8 cm from the vertex) and 16002 (pdg 2212, 41.9 cm, 0.0-39.8 cm). Vertex is good. Membership bookkeeping: nseg 6 = owner-grouped 6 = cmp_div 6, and the owner groups sum to 28 = the shard's n_seg, so the segment picture is complete. WHY 'unclear' -- TWO READINGS I COULD NOT SEPARATE: (a) 64033 is a correctly clustered compact EM shower: its four core segments (37 of its 42 fitted points) start 5.9 cm from the vertex and span 12.3 cm, its own point cloud is covered by the yellow member set at two azimuths, and nothing contiguous is left unclaimed in front of it. (b) 64033 is not an EM object at all: that same core hugs the unowned 41.9 cm proton 16002 along its whole length (minimum member-to-16002 distances 5.7 / 8.7 / 10.0 cm segment by segment, and 5.4-12.5 cm to the muon 16001), it is hook-shaped rather than conical, and 154 MeV inside a 12 cm core reads hadronic. I did NOT convert that into a PID flag, because the density argument here is exactly the kine_charge/skeleton-length shortcut correction 18 forbids and I have no independent width measurement of the blob charge -- the drawn point cloud around the member set is roughly 7 x 6 cm, which is compact but is a pixel estimate, not a measurement. Nothing was stolen from a neighbour under either reading: 16001 and 16002 are unowned by everything. THE MEMBERSHIP EDGE IS NOISY AND NON-MONOTONE, worth the owner's eye: on the acceptance plot the members include 47012 at (13.3 cm, 51.6 deg) and 48013 at (37.7 cm, 63.4 deg) -- both outside every pass-1 angle step (5 / 12.5 / 25 deg), taken by pass4_angle (direct) -- while the non-members 46011 at (18.0 cm, 34.1 deg) and 49014 at (31.2 cm, 52.1 deg) sit INSIDE the region those two were accepted from. So the gate accepted a 63 deg segment and rejected a 34 deg one on the same shower. Every one of the four is a 0.2-1.0 cm stub of 0.6-0.9 MeV, i.e. sub-1% of 154 MeV, which is why this does not move the verdict; 48013 in particular is 3 points sitting alone in empty space across a ~20 cm void and is the single thing I would mark OUT if I were marking. I recorded no marks, to keep the record consistent with the radio (pilot 5). pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event' and the capture produced no pi0 frames (no second gamma candidate to slot); nothing stored. NOT LOOKED AT: the 19 out-of-scope showers, all <= 15.2 MeV and 16 of them flagged 'conn 4: dropped by the PF tree' -- this event's shower list is mostly PF-tree debris. This verdict is about clustering of 64033; reading (b) above is the only PID doubt and it is explicitly NOT recorded as a PID verdict.

[agent-bulk] READ THIS FIRST: the verdict radio is stored on 19010 because correction 17 fixes the verdict shower as the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object (19010, 128.7 MeV, vs 33038 at 111.8), but the under-clustering claim is about the PAIR -- 19010 and 33038 look like two pieces of one forward EM object, and it is 33038 that is missing 19010, not the other way round. 19010 itself has nothing in front of it. THE FINDING: from the main vertex a single ray runs out and carries two reconstructed showers on it -- 33038 (111.8 MeV, 9 seg) with member points 54-90 cm from the vertex, then nothing at all, then 19010 (128.7 MeV, 2 seg) with member points 160-190.6 cm. The two vertex chords are 2.4 deg apart; measured from 33038's own start, 19010 sits at 105.7 cm / 5.5 deg with the code's own TIER 2 and 19011 at 135.0 cm / 7.1 deg TIER 3, and neither was absorbed. If they are one object the shower is ~240 MeV rather than 111.8. 33038 is unambiguously an EM shower in the picture: it opens out of its start into a branching cone with a wide point cloud, PCA 31.2 cm long, transverse RMS 2.31 cm, max radius 9.1 cm. THE COUNTER-READING, which is why this is 'unclear': there is 74 cm of ZERO charge between the two (minimum member-to-member distance 74.4 cm), so nothing grey or contiguous is being left behind -- the brief's strong under-clustering case does not apply, and the merge is only defensible as 'a hard bremsstrahlung photon from the first shower re-converted downstream', which is physically possible but is an inference, not something I can see. And 19010 is suspicious on its own terms: it is narrow and does not widen (PCA 30.9 cm, transverse RMS 0.91 cm, max radius 3.2 cm, flat quarter-by-quarter profile 1.25/0.75/0.62/0.67, largest internal gap 0.6 cm) and it hugs the TPC corner -- its points run x -199.0 to -194.4 (i.e. ~1 cm off the anode) and z 470.0 to 492.6, so it is leaving the active volume and I am only seeing ~31 cm of it. I did NOT record a PID verdict on it: at 128.7 MeV a young shower is only ~4 critical energies and can genuinely look narrow over 2.2 radiation lengths, unlike evt392901's 79 cm case. So the two readings are (a) one ~240 MeV EM object split by the gate = under-clustered, which is what I recorded, and (b) 33038 is a complete shower and 19010 is an unrelated MIP-like object exiting at the TPC corner, in which case both are correct as they stand. MARKS: 19010 and 19011 marked IN on shower 33038. Per correction 7 they differ in strength -- 19010 is the strong one (32.2 cm, 62 fitted points, tier 2 at 5.5 deg) and 19011 is the weak one (3.7 cm, 7 points, tier 3 at 135 cm) that I would let the owner reverse on its own. Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames (r95 185.9 cm): the star sits on the junction of the 78.7 cm unowned track 15001 and the green pion 15047, with a small charge cloud around it -- plausible, and in any case the finding above is measured from 33038's start, so correction 14 applies. Membership bookkeeping is consistent: 19010 nseg 2 = owner-grouped 2 = cmp_div 2; 33038 nseg 9 = 9 = 9; owner groups sum to 25 = the shard's n_seg. pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event'; the auto-slotted [19010, 33038] pair is the correction-3 artifact and its 'mass' of 5.0 (vertex) / 21.7 (axis) MeV is exactly the point -- at 2.4 deg apart these two cannot be a pi0's two gammas (a 240 MeV pi0 has a minimum opening angle near 68 deg), which is itself an argument that they are one object rather than two. Nothing stored. NOT LOOKED AT: the 9 out-of-scope showers, all <= 12.6 MeV; and 15047 (pdg 211, in scope) beyond noting it is the vertex pion.

[agent-bulk] verdict shower 9039 (pdg 11, kine_charge 166.5 MeV, 12 seg, 45.5 cm) -- the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; nothing in the event outranks it. It IS a real EM shower: 88 member points spanning 0-39.1 cm from the vertex at 0.0-12.9 deg, and the transverse RMS grows along it quarter by quarter, 0.54 -> 2.16 -> 2.17 -> 2.26 cm (max radius 4.5 cm) -- a narrow stem opening into a cone, which is what an electron should look like. THE FINDING (this is the strong grey-charge case, not the owned-by-a-neighbour one): segment 9038 is UNOWNED -- owner '-' in the segments source, the only unowned segment in the event -- and it is 15.3 cm long with 26 fitted points running from the main vertex out to 14.5 cm, inside 9039's own cone (its direction is 11.1 deg from 9039's axis, its midpoint sits at 8.9 deg, and 9039's accepted members span 0-12.9 deg). It is contiguous with the shower along its ENTIRE length: point by point, the distance from each of its 26 points to the nearest 9039 member point is 0.00, 0.30, 0.60 ... rising to a maximum of 2.01 cm at 10.4 cm out and falling back to 0.66 cm at its far end. So this is not a separate prong that happens to leave the same vertex -- it never gets more than 2 cm away. The shower already absorbs seven track-PID'd segments (9007 pdg 211, 9040 / 50025 / 52030 / 53031 / 38024 pdg 13, 52029 pdg 211) at 5-12 deg, so leaving 9038 out because it carries pdg 211 would be inconsistent with the reco's own behaviour on this shower. 9038 is marked IN on 9039; it is the only mark and it is the strong kind (26 points, 15.3 cm, touching). WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: if 9038 and 9039's seed are two skeletons threaded through ONE charge column (an imaging artifact rather than two particles), then its blobs may already be inside the shower's charge and merging would double-count rather than recover energy. I cannot separate that from a genuine second track at this zoom -- they overlap in every projection I have -- so the claim I am making is exactly the brief's under-clustering definition (unowned charge, contiguous, inside the cone) and no more. Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames (r95 345.1 cm, and note event_half_span_cm is saturated at 400.0 per correction 19 so the vtx-* set is useless here): the star sits at the head of the shower with the small 9033 stub on the other side; 9039 and 9033 are 174.9 deg apart, i.e. back-to-back through the vertex, which is the evt175896 shape from the pilot -- but here the back side is only 50.5 MeV in 6.1 cm against a 39 cm widening cone on the front side, so I read it as an electron plus small backward vertex activity rather than one line split in two, and I did not call vertex-bad. In any case the finding above is measured from the shower start and is vertex-independent (correction 14). OTHER SHOWERS: 9033 (pdg 11, 50.5 MeV, 2 seg) not separately judged beyond the back-to-back note; its far member 34020 sits at 38.5 cm / 162.3 deg from 9039, i.e. well behind, so it is not a candidate for 9039. Membership bookkeeping: nseg 12 = owner-grouped 12 = cmp_div 12, and the owner groups sum to 29 = the shard's n_seg. pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event'; the auto-slotted [9039, 9033] pair is the correction-3 artifact and at 173.1 deg apart it is not a pi0 topology; nothing stored. NOT LOOKED AT: the 14 out-of-scope showers, all <= 7.8 MeV, 9 of them flagged 'conn 4: dropped by the PF tree' and several 150-435 cm from the shower. This verdict is about clustering and is silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] VERTEX RESULT -- per the rubric I judged the vertex first, it fires, and this event therefore carries NO clustering judgement. Verdict shower 75005 (pdg 11, kine_charge 104.6 MeV, 5 seg, 49.3 cm), the only pdg-11 object in scope; passed over 29001, which is pdg 13 and whose kine_best 112.3 exceeds 104.6 even though its kine_charge is only 65.0. Vertex judged off the vtx-* set at +-114 cm: r95 is 91.2 cm here, below the 150 cm trigger, so scanbot_capture2 correctly wrote no vtxz-* frames and the ordinary sweep is already close in. THE FINDING: the blue star sits in the MIDDLE of a single straight, narrow, ~140 cm line, with nothing else converging on it. On one side of the star, segment 20000 is UNOWNED (the only unowned segment in the event) -- pdg 13, 71.7 cm, 120 fitted points, its closest point 0.0 cm from the star and its far end at 70.2 cm. On the other side, 75005's own member chain runs from 4.7 cm out to 73.4 cm. Their directions agree to 5.8 deg, the candidate table records 20000 at 173.5 deg from 75005's axis (i.e. exactly back-to-back), and the minimum separation between the two point sets is 4.7 cm, which is simply the gap at the star. I checked this at two azimuths and one elevation (vtx-az-055-el+20, vtx-az+065-el+20, vtx-az-055-el+60) precisely because a projection can hide a kink: in all three it is one continuous narrow line through the star, and the ONLY kink anywhere in the event is at the far end of 20000, about 105 cm from the star, where 29001 (pdg 13, 35.8 cm) bends away. Nothing else is at the star -- the remaining three objects are single-point stubs of 0.12-1.35 MeV lying 115-133 cm away. A neutrino vertex with two exactly back-to-back collinear track halves and no recoil prong is not an interaction topology, so the reading I favour is that this is a through-going track with the vertex placed in its middle; that is the same shape as pilot 2.4 (evt175896), and 'undecidable' is what the bucket is for. WHAT THE OWNER SHOULD ASK NEXT: if the vertex is judged right after all, the next question on 75005 is PID, not clustering. Excluding its one 2-point outlier (61004 at 68.8 cm / 18.1 deg, i.e. 21 cm transverse), 75005's core is narrow and does not widen -- transverse RMS 1.30 / 1.04 / 1.27 cm in successive quarters, largest internal gap 6.9 cm -- and its dominant member 78008 is a pdg-13 segment of 36.8 cm carrying 63 of its 86 points. That reads as a MIP, not a 105 MeV shower. I did NOT record that as a PID verdict, because the rubric stops on the vertex and one saved radio cannot carry both. No marks recorded: marking 20000 IN on 75005 would assert the two halves are one shower, which is the opposite of what I believe (they are one TRACK, and the vertex is what is wrong). pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event' and there is no second gamma candidate, so the capture wrote no pi0 frames; nothing stored. NOT LOOKED AT: the 3 out-of-scope showers, all <= 1.35 MeV.

[agent-bulk] REVISED IN SESSION (correction 10): the verdict and confidence are unchanged, but the first version of this note rested the call on a PCA transverse RMS, which pilot 1.2 warns is the scatter of the fitted SKELETON points, not the width of the charge -- it says that failure mode bit twice. The evidence below is re-ordered so the picture and the radiation-length argument carry it and the PCA is only corroboration. PID VERDICT -- and per correction 6 this event carries NO clustering judgement: I am not saying the clustering of 15008 is right or wrong, only that the object it collected is not an EM shower. Verdict shower 15008 (reco pdg 11, kine_charge 196.6 MeV, ONE segment, 85.9 cm, 144 fitted points), the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; passed over 15011 (pdg 13, 216.1 cm, kine_charge 307.9 / kine_best 445.0) and the pdg-13 objects 127030, 23017, 125023. WHY NOT AN EM SHOWER, strongest first. (1) THE DRAWN CHARGE. At two orthogonal azimuths (shw15008-az-055-el+20 and shw15008-az+085-el+20) the blue point cloud around this object is a thin uniform band from end to end, the same visual width as the muon 15011 and the other tracks in the same frames, with no cone, no branching and no fan anywhere along it. That is the judgement, made from the picture. (2) RADIATION LENGTHS. The object is 79 cm long, i.e. ~5.7 radiation lengths in liquid argon, and a 197 MeV electromagnetic shower must reach its maximum inside the first ~1-2 X0 and be visibly opening toward a ~10 cm Moliere radius long before the far end. Nothing about it changes over its whole length -- there is no stage at which it looks different from its start. (3) IT DOES NOT COME FROM THE VERTEX. Its closest member point is 34.9 cm from the star, and the angle between the (vertex -> start) chord and its own (start -> end) direction is 77.4 deg, so it is not a photon radiated from the neutrino vertex either. (4) CORROBORATION ONLY, with the caveat stated: a PCA over its 144 skeleton points gives length 79.4 cm, transverse RMS 1.49 cm, max radius 3.2 cm, largest along-axis gap 0.6 cm, and a flat quarter-by-quarter profile (1.81 / 1.48 / 1.04 / 1.52 cm). Those numbers describe the skeleton's wiggle, not the blob width, so on their own they could not distinguish a narrow track from a shower whose charge is wider than its skeleton -- they are quoted because the FLATNESS of the profile is still meaningful (a shower's skeleton branches as it develops; this one does not) and because they agree with (1). I did NOT price this with kine_charge / skeleton length, which is the shortcut correction 18 forbids. Vertex judged off the automatic vtxz-* 60 cm frames (r95 254 cm): the star sits on the junction of the 15011 muon and the long unowned grey track in a very dense multi-track region; plausible, and not needed, since the call above is measured from the object's own points and is vertex-independent (correction 14). THE SECOND EM CANDIDATE, deliberately NOT resolved: 15010 (pdg 11, kine_charge 106.1 MeV, 2 seg) PCAs to 35.4 cm with transverse RMS 1.31 cm and appears as a narrow hairpin with a short parallel stub (15014, 8.0 cm) beside it. But 35.4 cm is only ~2.5 radiation lengths and 106 MeV is ~3 critical energies, so the young-shower caveat applies -- a shower that young can genuinely look narrow, which is exactly why I declined a PID verdict on evt397630's 19010 (128.7 MeV over 2.2 X0). 15008 at 5.7 X0 is a different case and that difference is the whole argument. So: 15010 is not separately resolved, and I make NO claim that this 'other_em' event contains no EM shower -- only that its leading pdg-11 object is not one. UNOWNED CHARGE: three segments are grey (15005, pdg 211, 183.3 cm; 15007, pdg 211, 38.5 cm; 127032, pdg 13, 38.5 cm), all track-like and all at 98-156 deg from 15008's axis, so none is an under-clustering candidate for it. Membership bookkeeping is self-consistent: nseg 1 = owner-grouped 1 = cmp_div 1, and the owner groups sum to 22 = the shard's n_seg. pi0: kine_div says 'no pi0 group in this event'; the auto-slotted [15008, 15010] pair is the correction-3 artifact and I did not store it. NOT LOOKED AT: the 4 out-of-scope showers, all <= 14.1 MeV.
